references.text: Here a parallel is drawn to the confession of faith before others and how this is acknowledged by God, similar to Isaiah where it speaks of not fearing human judgment when one has the Lord's support.
This verse reflects the idea of testifying to God's laws before kings without shame, which corresponds to confessing faith before people in Matthew.
In Hebrews we find a similar exhortation to hold fast to our confession of hope without wavering, which recalls the confession before people in Matthew.
1 John speaks of confessing the Son so as to have the Father, mirroring the idea of mutual confession before people and before God in Matthew.
